lines: Two answers are still needed from you, each a yes or no. One, take the level line's mend, which shows on the live page at low quality only. Two, take the two what-ifs that both fresh reviewers said to take: fall's lit faces going out before winter's base comes, and summer's sand mound breaking up as it leaves. You can answer the second by eye, because Preview 12 will show the whole film with those two in.

Your word of 10:22 AM MT is in: render the low resolution film. I take it as move on to the film with no further round of looks, and I start no new look work. The film was ordered at 10:37 AM MT on five machines: the whole piece with the prompt opening and its sound, 960 x 540 at 30 frames a second, at the fast draft setting. It comes here as Preview 11 by about 11:45 AM MT, an estimate from the last draft's pace. Preview 11 is the main branch as it stands, without the level line's mend and without the what-ifs. Preview 12 is the same film with the two what-ifs in. No 4K render is started or handed over on these words. That waits for your word after you have watched.
Phases 0 to 5 are complete. Phase 6, the films and delivery, is open.

Landed since the last status. The render instructions for your PC had their third cold read by a fresh reader: an agent can follow the file alone once three points are mended, score 7 of 10, all eleven gates met by its read. Two points are real traps: step 2 begun from the wrong folder, and your approval words typed inside quotes. Both are being mended now, then one hosted proof runs on the mended file. It goes onto the main branch only when that proof passes in every row and the same reader says yes.

The what-if for summer's lights during the shake has its first seven after frames at 4K, three pictures attached. The flat squares are gone in all five frames that should change, and the two frames that should stay are the same bit for bit. What stands in their place reads as fine sparks in the whole frame and as cut sticks with square ends at full size, and one frame shows a row of white dots along the glass's foot. Its builder has that list. Nothing is ruled. The other seven frames and the motion proof are being drawn, then two fresh reviewers judge it, and it reaches you only if both say take it.
Not offered: the what-if for fall's lifted leaves at the landing. Its second try failed its own measure, so the film keeps the main branch there.

The page that loses its drawing on hosted Macs, open items 294 and 295, measured on hosted Macs only. The engine of Safari kept the drawing in 12 of 12 loads. A second kind of hosted Mac lost it in 2 of 15 loads against 44 of 71 on the first kind, so it follows the machine more than the page. After a loss the browser itself blocks the page for two minutes, which explains the refusals seen. The hosted run that could not end green ended as cancelled, as I said it would, so GitHub may have mailed you. On a real Mac, a real graphics card or a phone nothing is measured.

Open and awaited in Mountain Time, by my orders' limits. Preview 11 and Preview 12 about 11:45 AM. The lights' motion proof about 11:30 AM and its builder's report 11:50 AM. The lost drawing's ten must items 11:45 AM, then a second fresh reviewer before anything merges. The sand mound's arrival, its one mend, about 11:55 AM. The hosted Mac report's second version 12:30 PM. The render instructions' mend and proof, time not known yet. The veil's what-if by 1:45 PM.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. First the low resolution film, Preview 11 and Preview 12, today. Then the render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code. The what-ifs still in work, each shown before and after at 4K with the reviewers' words. On his word after the film: the freeze, the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last the fresh review and BUILD COMPLETE. Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger at 10:41 AM MT Saturday, 52 rows, the last call 10:47 PM MT Wednesday).
